setting: A student talks with a residence hall assistant about laundry machines that will not accept her laundry card.
narrator_intro: Listen to a conversation between a student and a residence hall assistant.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Hi. The washers on the second floor won't take my laundry card. The reader just blinks red.

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Yeah, we've had reports since this morning. Building Services thinks the card readers lost connection after last night's power blip.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: I have a huge pile of clothes and a lab coat I need clean for tomorrow. Is there another floor I can use?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: The fourth-floor machines are working. You'll need to take the elevator—the stairwell door by laundry is temporarily locked for a fire-panel test until six.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Okay. Do I need to reload money on my card, or is the balance still there?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Your balance is fine. Just avoid machines two and three on two—those readers are offline. If a machine takes the card but doesn't start, don't swipe again; come back here and we'll refund the cycle.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Got it. How long until second floor is fixed?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: They said by tomorrow afternoon. I'll post a notice on the laundry door when it's back online.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Thanks. One more thing—can I borrow a spare laundry basket? Mine cracked.

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: We have two at the desk. Leave your student ID while you use it, and bring it back tonight.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Perfect. I'll head to fourth floor now.

narrator_outro: Now get ready to answer the questions.

questions.narrator_text: What is the conversation mainly about?

options.A: Moving the student to a new residence hall
options.B: Solving a laundry-card problem in the dorm
options.C: Buying a new washing machine for the building
options.D: Scheduling a fire drill for the whole campus

questions.explanation: Her laundry card readers fail on floor two; he redirects her and explains refunds and timing.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing D because a fire-panel test is mentioned—that only explains a locked stairwell.

questions.narrator_text: Where can the student do laundry right now?

options.A: Only in the student union basement
options.B: On the second floor using machines two and three
options.D: At the residence hall desk with a staff washer

questions.explanation: He says the fourth-floor machines are working.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing B—those second-floor readers are specifically offline.

questions.narrator_text: What should she do if a machine takes her card but does not start?

options.A: Swipe the card a second time immediately
options.B: Kick the machine to reset the reader
options.C: Return to the desk for a cycle refund and not swipe again
options.D: Add more money online before trying again

questions.explanation: He tells her not to swipe again and to come back for a refund of the cycle.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing A or D—balance is fine; double-swiping is what he warns against.

questions.narrator_text: What must she leave in order to borrow a laundry basket?

options.B: A cash deposit of ten dollars

questions.explanation: Spare baskets require leaving a student ID and returning the basket tonight.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing C because the talk is about laundry cards—the deposit item is the student ID.
